events.title: A Hospitaller fleet defeats the Aydinids off Chios
events.description: Off the Aegean island of Chios, a Christian fleet, mainly Hospitaller, sank 22 of 28 ships of the Turkish Aydinid emirate. It was only a temporary setback for the Aydinids, who had turned to piracy as Byzantine power collapsed.

events.title: Three hundred colonists sail from Dieppe for New France
events.description: Three hundred colonists bound for New France sailed from Dieppe, then the leading port of the French kingdom. The colony on the St Lawrence had its capital at Quebec, founded by Samuel de Champlain in 1608.

events.title: Riot greets Charles I's new prayer book in Edinburgh
events.description: Worshippers in St Giles' Cathedral protested violently when the new Scottish Book of Common Prayer was first read. The resistance led to the National Covenant, the Bishops' Wars and the British civil wars.
events.html: Worshippers in St Giles' Cathedral protested violently when the new Scottish Book of Common Prayer was first read. The resistance led to the National Covenant, the Bishops' Wars and the British civil wars.

events.title: Denmark–Norway captures the Swedish harbour town of Marstrand
events.description: A Dano-Norwegian siege of the Swedish harbour town of Marstrand, begun on 6 July, ended in its capture. In the Scanian War Denmark–Norway sought to recover the provinces lost in 1658, but the peace treaties of 1679 restored the pre-war borders.

events.title: Bonnie Prince Charlie lands on Eriskay
events.description: Charles Edward Stuart landed on the Hebridean island of Eriskay to reclaim the throne for his father. The Jacobite rising he launched ended in defeat at Culloden in April 1746.
events.html: Charles Edward Stuart landed on the Hebridean island of Eriskay to reclaim the throne for his father. The Jacobite rising he launched ended in defeat at Culloden in April 1746.

events.title: William Austin Burt patents his 'typographer'
events.description: Michigan surveyor William Austin Burt received a US patent for the typographer, a hand-operated printing machine. Slow and never sold commercially, it is often called the first American typewriter.

events.title: Egypt's Free Officers overthrow King Farouk
events.description: Army officers led by Muhammad Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser seized power in a bloodless coup, forcing King Farouk to abdicate days later. Egypt became a republic in 1953.
events.html: Army officers led by Muhammad Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser seized power in a bloodless coup, forcing King Farouk to abdicate days later. Egypt became a republic in 1953.

events.title: Greece's military junta collapses after the Cyprus crisis
events.description: Discredited by its coup in Cyprus and the Turkish invasion that followed, the Greek junta handed power to civilians. Konstantinos Karamanlis returned from exile the next day to restore democracy.
